findings.detail:
A full POST /Library/Refresh scan that re-adopts a local sidecar as an item's Primary image moves an owned session to OwnershipLost, and v1.2 exposes no in-product administrative action that returns the item to a publishable session: ArtworkRegenerationPlanner.IsPublicationBlocked blocks {OwnershipLost, OwnershipUnknown, RestorePending, RestoreBlocked}, and the restoration path (ArtworkPublisher -> PublishedArtworkStateTransitions.RequestRestore) only accepts State=Published. The badge is therefore not re-asserted after such a scan until an operator clears the session out of band. This is the documented fail-closed decision (docs/data-model/03-10-artworkcacheentry.md 3.10.4), not a defect, but there is no documented recovery trigger for a library whose operator routinely runs full scans. The second verifier pass confirmed the trap is durable and unrecoverable in-product: the movie item stayed in OwnershipLost across an Extra Large size change, a full provider outage and recovery, and a full host restart, and it was the sole reason the L4 row could not be closed. The verifier deliberately did not clear the state file out of band, because doing so would simulate an undocumented operator action rather than exercise the product.
 THIRD PASS (2026-09-29T12:05Z-12:11Z): re-confirmed that this is a library-refresh behaviour and not an Extra Large behaviour. On the fresh prefix /tmp/arrtags-21.4b, where the only POST /Library/VirtualFolders ... refreshLibrary=true was issued at library-add time before the first publication and no later full scan was ever run, all three items published and stayed State 1 (Published) with LastOwnershipObservation.Status 0 through the Medium baseline, the Renderer.Size=ExtraLarge save and a scheduled-task-triggered re-render; the previously blocked test movie 2e6e66205d333c0b0131d3312cd050a5 rendered normally to a new 18,029-byte Extra Large identity. The movie 9eee318fd9e81741cda2e4ab8b4c788c on the earlier contaminated prefix /tmp/arrtags-21.4 remains in OwnershipLost and was deliberately not touched, so this finding's substance is unchanged; only its attribution is now sharper - the trigger is the post-publication library scan, and the recommended operating discipline is to drive re-renders with POST /ScheduledTasks/Running/<ArrTags task id> instead.

findings.detail: Three v1.2 surfaces are not executable on the pinned host and were verified only against the served resource and the live endpoint, not by running their code: the settings page's unit conversion and modal reminder (no JavaScript runtime; --nowebclient), the diagnostics panel's unauthorized behaviour (same), and the Extra Large safe-area clamp/shorten-omit path (observable only on the owned items, one of which was blocked). The second pass additionally established that the step-multiple rejection is not reachable through the elevation-gated API at all: ADR-028 clause 1 assigns that check to the settings conversion path and the input's native step attribute, while the server's OperationalLimits.Validate deliberately enforces only the byte range, so a raw API POST of an off-step value (ProviderResponseLimitBytes=1572865) is accepted and stored as bytes without rescaling. That is the documented design, not a defect, but it means the step-multiple guarantee is a page-side behaviour only. All of this is consistent with the residuals already registered in docs/limitations/00-index.md (V12-G6-1, V12-G8-1, V12-G8-2) and with the bound recorded in ADR-028's implementation note.
evidence: ADR-028 clause 1: 'This step-multiple rejection is a new check introduced by this change, owned by task 16.1: the existing OperationalLimits.Validate enforces only the field's byte range, not step alignment, so the settings conversion/validation path (and, where the page uses native constraint validation, the input's step attribute) must add an explicit step check. The internal OperationalLimits byte-range validation is unchanged.'

Live: POST ProviderResponseLimitBytes=1572865 -> HTTP 204 and ArrTags.xml persists 1572865; POST 134217728 (over the 64-MiB max) and POST 1024 (under the 64-KiB min) each return HTTP 204 with an empty body and leave the previously persisted value unchanged, confirming the range check is enforced server-side while the step check is not.
The live host launched by scripts/provision-jellyfin-test-host.sh always passes --nowebclient, so /web/ConfigurationPage?name=ArrTags is served as a static resource with no client to run it.
findings.recommended_action: None required; the bound is already documented. Any future claim about the page conversion, the step-multiple rejection or the panel behaviour must keep the structural-only qualifier.
